messages:
maya-cs: Customer LexaPay reporting intermittent 502s from hosted API when sending large embedding batches. Started ~2026-03-15T15:02Z. They see ~5-10% of requests returning 502s, usually during bursts. Provided one trace id tid-6b9f and sample curl.
alex-sre: Can you paste the exact curl + trace id here? Need headers and payload size to triage.
maya-cs: curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings -H 'Authorization: Bearer <REDACTED>' -H 'Content-Type: application/json' -d '{"input": ["...long list..." ] }' --trace-ascii -
payload per request ~450-800KB depending on batch, they send ~6 concurrent requests during peak. trace_id=tid-6b9f
jay-ingress: Observing a spike of upstream resets on the edge proxies 15:01:34 -> 15:06:10 UTC. Envoy logs show: `upstream reset: connection failure` and `recvmsg error: Resource temporarily unavailable` for connections to runtime pool in us-east-1. Many half-closed HTTP/2 streams.
maria-runtime: On runtime side, shard-3 shows memory pressure and a handful of slow responses >90s that then get closed by upstream. No GPU OOMs but host RSS climbs. Looks correlated with large embedding batches arriving in parallel.
alex-sre: Two quick hypotheses: 1) ingress conn-pool / keepalive exhaustion leads to Envoy returning 502 when upstream reset; 2) large auth/payload headers or streaming behavior triggers runtime to stall and close connections. Any auth proxy logs?
maya-cs: Customer also on SSO, but auth service latency normal. They confirmed same token works with small payloads.
jay-ingress: Ingress NGINX/Envoy config currently: keepalive_requests 100; worker_connections 1024; proxy_read_timeout 60s. H2 window settings default. I'm seeing many connections stuck in CLOSE_WAIT. I'll push a canary change to increase proxy_read_timeout to 90s and bump worker_connections in canary to see impact.
alex-sre: Quick mitigations to try now: - route this customer's requests to model-embed-small (lighter memory) via routing policy - apply temporary per-key concurrency limit (reduce from 6 -> 2) - increase ingress timeouts and connpool sizes in canary - ask customer to shrink batches / backoff
maya-cs: Customer requested fast fix, accepted reduced concurrency for now while they work on batching.
sre-bot: deploy started: roll/ingress-timeout-and-conns by alex-sre (canary us-east-1). CI checks passed.
jay-ingress: Canary deployed. Early telemetry: 502 rate for LexaPay in canary decreased from 7.4% -> 1.1% over 10 minutes. Upstream reset logs reduced.
maria-runtime: We saw fewer long-lived requests after routing a subset to model-embed-small. However runtime shard memory still spikes on worst-case batches. I'll add a soft request-size guard to catch very large batch sizes and return 413/429 with guidance. Filing internal RTs.
alex-sre: Agreed on next steps: 1) infra: raise worker_connections and tune keepalive in prod; 2) runtime: implement soft quota for payload size and better OOM-safe error path; 3) product/docs: publish recommended batch size for embeddings and example chunking; 4) support: notify customer of temp limits and retry guidance.
maya-cs: I'll notify LexaPay: reduced concurrency applied, please retry with exponential backoff and split large batches. They replied their traffic is stable and reported no 502s in last 25m. Provided new trace tid-6b9f-2 which shows success.
alex-sre: Creating infra ticket INF-1187 to raise worker_connections and INF-1188 for global keepalive tuning. maria-runtime filed RT-5423 (soft quota) and RT-5424 (OOM watchdog).
jay-ingress: Will monitor canary -> scale to prod if steady. Will also add a metric alert for half-closed streams > 0.5% of connections.
alex-sre: Marking this support escalation as mitigated. Closing loop: make sure docs + rate-limits + routing policy are completed before customer fully unblocked. Reopen thread if reoccurs. :white_check_mark:
